subproblems.title: Null on every vanishing relatively compact open set implies null off the support
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, let T ∈ D_n(U) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), let M ⊆ ℝ^P with M ⊆ U, and let μ be any measure on ℝ^P (Eucl P). Suppose μ(M ∩ W) = 0 for every W ⊆ ℝ^P such that W is open, closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ U and T vanishes on W (T.VanishesOn W: T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W). Then μ(M ∖ spt T) = 0. Here spt T = T.support = U ∖ T.zeroRegion, and T.zeroRegion is the union of all such W.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)), M ⊆ U → (∀ W : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen W → IsCompact (closure W) → closure W ⊆ U → T.VanishesOn W → μ (M ∩ W) = 0) → μ (M \ T.support) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent proof (the countable union). Here it is stated for an arbitrary measure μ, with the local nullity of step 7 taken as a hypothesis. Siblings used: none.

The Lean statement is identical to that of the accepted DAG node root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.rectifiable_support_null-a1.support_null_reduction-a1 (lpf_rsn_null_diff_support_of_local_null). This child keeps a fresh name, as this run does for other identical types, so the branch has no cross-branch dependency. The proof below is self-contained.

Conventions.
- ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) carries its usual metric topology, which is second countable.
- μ is applied to arbitrary subsets as an outer measure. Only monotonicity and countable subadditivity are used.
- "T vanishes on W" (T.VanishesOn W) means T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
- 𝒲 is the family of all W ⊆ ℝ^P such that W is open, closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ U and T vanishes on W.
- By the SimonGMT definitions GeometricCurrentOn.zeroRegion and GeometricCurrentOn.support (Simon Ch. 6, 2.11): T.zeroRegion = ⋃₀ 𝒲 and spt T = T.support = U ∖ T.zeroRegion.

1. (M ∖ spt T ⊆ T.zeroRegion.) Let x ∈ M with x ∉ T.support. Since M ⊆ U, x ∈ U. If x ∉ T.zeroRegion, then x ∈ U ∖ T.zeroRegion = T.support, a contradiction. Hence x ∈ T.zeroRegion.

2. (A countable subfamily with the same union.) Every member of 𝒲 is open and ℝ^P is second countable. By the Lindelöf property of second-countable spaces (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable) there is a countable subfamily 𝒲₀ ⊆ 𝒲 with ⋃₀ 𝒲₀ = ⋃₀ 𝒲 = T.zeroRegion.

3. (Covering.) Let x ∈ M ∖ T.support. By steps 1 and 2, x ∈ ⋃₀ 𝒲₀, so x ∈ W for some W ∈ 𝒲₀. Since also x ∈ M, x ∈ W ∩ M. Hence M ∖ T.support ⊆ ⋃_{W ∈ 𝒲₀} (W ∩ M).

4. (Each piece is null.) Let W ∈ 𝒲₀. Then W ∈ 𝒲, so W is open, closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ U and T vanishes on W. The hypothesis gives μ(M ∩ W) = 0, i.e. μ(W ∩ M) = 0.

5. (Conclusion.) 𝒲₀ is countable, so countable subadditivity and step 4 give μ(⋃_{W ∈ 𝒲₀} (W ∩ M)) = 0 (Mathlib measure_biUnion_null_iff). By step 3 and monotonicity (measure_mono_null), μ(M ∖ T.support) = 0. ∎

```lean
theorem iwl_sp_sn_null_diff_support_of_local_null : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)), M ⊆ U → (∀ W : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen W → IsCompact (closure W) → closure W ⊆ U → T.VanishesOn W → μ (M ∩ W) = 0) → μ (M \ T.support) = 0 := by
  intro P n U T M μ hMU hloc
  obtain ⟨S', hS'c, hS'S, hS'eq⟩ := TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable
    {W : Set (Eucl P) | IsOpen W ∧ IsCompact (closure W) ∧ closure W ⊆ U ∧ T.VanishesOn W}
    (fun W hW => hW.1)
  have hsub : M \ T.support ⊆ ⋃ W ∈ S', W ∩ M := by
    intro x ⟨hxM, hxs⟩
    have hxZ : x ∈ T.zeroRegion := by
      by_contra hx
      exact hxs ⟨hMU hxM, hx⟩
    have hxZ' : x ∈ ⋃₀ S' := by
      rw [hS'eq]; exact hxZ
    obtain ⟨W, hW, hxW⟩ := hxZ'
    exact Set.mem_biUnion hW ⟨hxW, hxM⟩
  refine measure_mono_null hsub ?_
  rw [measure_biUnion_null_iff hS'c]
  intro W hW
  obtain ⟨hWo, hWc, hWU, hWv⟩ := hS'S hW
  rw [Set.inter_comm]
  exact hloc W hWo hWc hWU hWv
```
proof_key_steps: Since M ⊆ U, every x ∈ M ∖ spt T lies in T.zeroRegion = ⋃₀𝒲. Here 𝒲 is the family of open W with compact closure inside U on which T vanishes.
By second countability (Lindelöf, TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable), a countable subfamily 𝒲₀ ⊆ 𝒲 has the same union.
Hence M ∖ spt T ⊆ ⋃_{W∈𝒲₀} (W ∩ M), and each μ(M ∩ W) = 0 by hypothesis.
Countable subadditivity (measure_biUnion_null_iff) and monotonicity (measure_mono_null) give μ(M ∖ spt T) = 0.

subproblems.title: Finitely many n-covectors separate n-vectors
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ there are N ∈ ℕ and n-covectors b_1, …, b_N ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n, i.e. continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ, with the following property. Every n-vector w ∈ NVector (Eucl P) n (a continuous linear functional on Covector (Eucl P) n) with w(b_i) = 0 for all i is the zero functional.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ (N : ℕ) (b : Fin N → Covector (Eucl P) n), ∀ w : NVector (Eucl P) n, (∀ i, w (b i) = 0) → w = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (a finite separating family of covectors). Finite-dimensionality of the covector space is proved here because the frozen import closure has no FiniteDimensional instance for Covector (Eucl P) n. Siblings used: none.

The Lean statement is identical to that of the accepted DAG node root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.rectifiable_support_null-a1.covector_separating_family-a1 (lpf_rsn_covector_separating_family). This child keeps a fresh name, as this run does for other identical types, so the branch has no cross-branch dependency. The proof below is self-contained.

Conventions.
- Covector (Eucl P) n = (ℝ^P)[⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ is the space of continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ. Its addition and scalar multiplication are pointwise.
- NVector (Eucl P) n = Covector (Eucl P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ is the space of continuous linear functionals on covectors.
- e_1, …, e_P is the standard basis of ℝ^P (Mathlib (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).toBasis).

1. (Coordinates.) Define Φ : Covector (Eucl P) n → ℝ^(Fin n → Fin P) by Φ(α)(r) := α(e_{r(1)}, …, e_{r(n)}) for r : Fin n → Fin P. For every tuple v, (α + β)(v) = α(v) + β(v) and (c·α)(v) = c·α(v), both by definition. Hence Φ is ℝ-linear.

2. (Φ is injective.) Suppose Φ(α) = Φ(β). Then the multilinear maps underlying α and β agree on every tuple (e_{r(1)}, …, e_{r(n)}) of basis vectors. A multilinear map on a finite family of modules with bases is determined by these values. Write v_i = Σ_k v_i(k)·e_k and expand by multilinearity:
   α(v_1, …, v_n) = Σ_{r : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_i v_i(r(i)))·α(e_{r(1)}, …, e_{r(n)}),
   and likewise for β (Mathlib Module.Basis.ext_multilinear, with the basis e in every slot). Hence α(v) = β(v) for every v ∈ (ℝ^P)ⁿ, so α = β.

3. (Finite dimension and a basis.) ℝ^(Fin n → Fin P) is a finite product of copies of ℝ, hence finite-dimensional. Φ is an injective linear map into it, so Covector (Eucl P) n is finite-dimensional (Mathlib FiniteDimensional.of_injective). Let N := finrank_ℝ Covector (Eucl P) n and let b_1, …, b_N be a basis of Covector (Eucl P) n (Mathlib Module.finBasis).

4. (Separation.) Let w ∈ NVector (Eucl P) n with w(b_i) = 0 for every i. Every covector α can be written α = Σ_i c_i·b_i with real c_i, so linearity gives w(α) = Σ_i c_i·w(b_i) = 0. Equivalently, the linear maps w and 0 agree on a basis and are therefore equal (Mathlib Module.Basis.ext). Hence w(α) = 0 for every α, i.e. w = 0 as a continuous linear map. ∎

Edge cases (covered by the argument above, no separate treatment needed):
- n = 0: the domain of Φ is the space of constants and the codomain is ℝ^(one point).
- P = 0 and n ≥ 1: the codomain is the zero space, so Φ injective means Covector (Eucl P) n = 0 and N = 0. The separation statement then holds because every w on the zero space is 0.

It was placed inside `namespace Submission`, immediately before `theorem main_theorem`, in a scratch copy of GMT/Ch06/Submission.lean. `#print axioms` gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The comparator's generated NodeSolution module (`exact Submission.iwl_sp_sn_covector_separating_family`) typechecks.

```lean
theorem iwl_sp_sn_covector_separating_family : ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ (N : ℕ) (b : Fin N → Covector (Eucl P) n), ∀ w : NVector (Eucl P) n, (∀ i, w (b i) = 0) → w = 0 := by
  intro P n
  let e : Module.Basis (Fin P) ℝ (Eucl P) := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).toBasis
  let Φ : Covector (Eucl P) n →ₗ[ℝ] ((Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ) :=
    { toFun := fun α r => α (fun i => e (r i))
      map_add' := fun _ _ => rfl
      map_smul' := fun _ _ => rfl }
  have hΦ : Function.Injective Φ := by
    intro α β h
    have hm : α.toContinuousMultilinearMap.toMultilinearMap =
        β.toContinuousMultilinearMap.toMultilinearMap :=
      Module.Basis.ext_multilinear (fun _ => e) (fun r => congrFun h r)
    ext v
    exact congrArg (fun m : MultilinearMap ℝ (fun _ : Fin n => Eucl P) ℝ => m v) hm
  have : FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Eucl P) n) := FiniteDimensional.of_injective Φ hΦ
  let b := Module.finBasis ℝ (Covector (Eucl P) n)
  refine ⟨Module.finrank ℝ (Covector (Eucl P) n), b, ?_⟩
  intro w hw
  have hlin : (w : Covector (Eucl P) n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) = 0 := b.ext (fun i => by simpa using hw i)
  ext α
  simpa using congrArg (fun l : Covector (Eucl P) n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ => l α) hlin
```
proof_key_steps: The coordinate map Φ(α)(r) := α(e_{r(1)}, …, e_{r(n)}) is linear from covectors to the finite-dimensional space ℝ^(Fin n → Fin P).
Φ is injective, because a multilinear map is determined by its values on tuples of basis vectors (Module.Basis.ext_multilinear).
Hence Covector (Eucl P) n is finite-dimensional (FiniteDimensional.of_injective). Take a basis b_1, …, b_N (Module.finBasis).
A linear functional that vanishes on a basis is zero (Module.Basis.ext).

subproblems.title: A signed simple n-vector of an orthonormal frame has evaluation bound 1 and is nonzero
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ : Fin n → Eucl P) (w : NVector (Eucl P) n), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (w = simpleNVector τ ∨ w = -simpleNVector τ) → (∀ b : Covector (Eucl P) n, |w b| ≤ ‖b‖) ∧ w ≠ 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1(a) and 1(b) of the parent proof, the pointwise algebra at a good point x with τ orthonormal and ξ(x) = ±τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_n. Here w plays the role of ξ(x). Siblings used: none.

Conventions.
- For b ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n, ‖b‖ is the operator norm of the continuous alternating map. Hence |b(v_1, …, v_n)| ≤ ‖b‖·Π_i ‖v_i‖ for every tuple v (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).
- simpleNVector τ is the continuous linear functional b ↦ b(τ) = b(τ_1, …, τ_n) (SimonGMT simpleNVector_apply, true by definition).
- innerSL ℝ u : ℝ^P →L[ℝ] ℝ is the functional v ↦ ⟨u, v⟩ (Mathlib innerSL_apply_apply).
- wedgeCovectors n α is the exterior product of the 1-covectors α_1, …, α_n. SimonGMT wedgeCovectors_apply_det states wedgeCovectors n α (v) = det(α_i(v_j))_{i,j}.

1. (Evaluation.) Let b be an n-covector. If w = simpleNVector τ then w(b) = b(τ). If w = −simpleNVector τ then w(b) = −b(τ). In both cases |w(b)| = |b(τ)|.

2. (Bound, part (i).) Orthonormality gives ‖τ_i‖ = 1 for every i, so Π_i ‖τ_i‖ = 1 (for n = 0 the empty product is 1). Hence |b(τ)| ≤ ‖b‖·Π_i ‖τ_i‖ = ‖b‖. By step 1, |w(b)| ≤ ‖b‖ for every n-covector b.

3. (A test covector.) Put b_τ := wedgeCovectors n (i ↦ innerSL ℝ τ_i). By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, b_τ(τ) = det A, where A_{ij} = innerSL ℝ τ_i (τ_j) = ⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩. By orthonormality, ⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩ = 1 if i = j and 0 otherwise (Mathlib orthonormal_iff_ite). So A is the n × n identity matrix and b_τ(τ) = det 1 = 1 (Mathlib Matrix.det_one; for n = 0 the empty determinant is 1).

4. (Nonvanishing, part (ii).) Suppose w = 0. Steps 1 and 3 then give 0 = |0(b_τ)| = |w(b_τ)| = |b_τ(τ)| = |1| = 1, a contradiction. Hence w ≠ 0. ∎

Formalization aid (not part of the mathematical argument). The following Lean proof of exactly this frozen statement compiled with Lean v4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 25730c7c, frozen project d8d46c9 and the shared pinned packages. It was placed inside `namespace Submission`, immediately before `theorem main_theorem`, in a scratch copy of GMT/Ch06/Submission.lean. `#print axioms` gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The comparator's generated NodeSolution module (`exact Submission.iwl_sp_sn_signed_simpleNVector_bound_ne_zero`) typechecks.

```lean
theorem iwl_sp_sn_signed_simpleNVector_bound_ne_zero : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ : Fin n → Eucl P) (w : NVector (Eucl P) n), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (w = simpleNVector τ ∨ w = -simpleNVector τ) → (∀ b : Covector (Eucl P) n, |w b| ≤ ‖b‖) ∧ w ≠ 0 := by
  intro P n τ w hτ hw
  have habs : ∀ b : Covector (Eucl P) n, |w b| = |b τ| := by
    intro b
    rcases hw with rfl | rfl
    · simp
    · simp
  have hbound : ∀ b : Covector (Eucl P) n, |b τ| ≤ ‖b‖ := by
    intro b
    have h1 := b.le_opNorm τ
    have hprod : ∏ i, ‖τ i‖ = 1 := Finset.prod_eq_one (fun i _ => hτ.1 i)
    rw [hprod, mul_one, Real.norm_eq_abs] at h1
    exact h1
  refine ⟨fun b => (habs b).trans_le (hbound b), ?_⟩
  intro h0
  have hdet : wedgeCovectors n (fun i => innerSL ℝ (τ i)) τ = 1 := by
    rw [wedgeCovectors_apply_det]
    have hm : (Matrix.of fun i j => (innerSL ℝ (τ i)) (τ j)) = (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) := by
      ext i j
      rw [Matrix.of_apply, innerSL_apply_apply, orthonormal_iff_ite.mp hτ i j, Matrix.one_apply]
    rw [hm, Matrix.det_one]
  have h1 := habs (wedgeCovectors n (fun i => innerSL ℝ (τ i)))
  rw [h0, hdet] at h1
  simp at h1
```
proof_key_steps: |w(b)| = |b(τ_1, …, τ_n)| for every covector b, whatever the sign.
|b(τ)| ≤ ‖b‖·Π_i‖τ_i‖ = ‖b‖, because ‖τ_i‖ = 1 (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).
b_τ := wedgeCovectors n (i ↦ innerSL ℝ τ_i) satisfies b_τ(τ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = det 1 = 1 (wedgeCovectors_apply_det, orthonormal_iff_ite).
If w = 0, then 0 = |w(b_τ)| = |b_τ(τ)| = 1, a contradiction. So w ≠ 0.

subproblems.title: Fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations with a positive weight on a set
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (M W : Set (Eucl P)) (θ g : Eucl P → ℝ) (C : ℝ), IsOpen W → NullMeasurableSet M μ → (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x) → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ W) μ → AEStronglyMeasurable g (μ.restrict M) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict M), |g x| ≤ C) → (∀ φ : Eucl P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) φ → HasCompactSupport φ → tsupport φ ⊆ W → ∫ x in M, θ x * (φ x * g x) ∂μ = 0) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict M), x ∈ W → g x = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4 and 6 of the parent proof (integrable coefficients and the fundamental lemma), with ν = μ⌞M. The coefficient x ↦ ξ(x)(b) is replaced by a general function g, and its a.e. bound ‖b‖ by a constant C. Siblings used: none.

The Lean statement is identical to that of the accepted DAG node root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.rectifiable_support_null-a1.weighted_fundamental_lemma-a1 (lpf_rsn_weighted_fundamental_lemma). This child keeps a fresh name, as this run does for other identical types, so the branch has no cross-branch dependency. The proof below is self-contained.

Conventions.
- ℝ^P = Eucl P carries its Borel σ-algebra.
- μ⌞S := μ.restrict S and ∫_S h dμ := ∫ h d(μ⌞S).
- "C^∞" means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), which is Mathlib's smoothness order ∞ (all finite orders). The fundamental lemma below is stated with this order.

1. (Restriction identity.) W is open, hence measurable. So (μ⌞M)⌞W = μ⌞(W ∩ M) = μ⌞(M ∩ W) (Mathlib Measure.restrict_restrict).

2. (f := θ·g is integrable on W for μ⌞M.)
   - By (ii), θ is integrable for μ⌞(M ∩ W).
   - μ⌞(M ∩ W) ≤ μ⌞M (Measure.restrict_mono), so by (iii) g is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞(M ∩ W).
   - M ∩ W ⊆ M, so by (iv) |g(x)| ≤ C for μ⌞(M ∩ W)-a.e. x (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset).
   - An integrable function times an a.e.-strongly measurable, a.e.-bounded function is integrable (Mathlib Integrable.mul_bdd). Equivalently, f is a.e.-strongly measurable with |f| ≤ C·|θ| a.e. and C·|θ| is integrable (Integrable.mono').
   So f is integrable for μ⌞(M ∩ W) = (μ⌞M)⌞W, i.e. IntegrableOn f W (μ⌞M). In particular f is locally integrable on W for μ⌞M (IntegrableOn.locallyIntegrableOn).
   No sign condition on C is needed: Integrable.mul_bdd has none, and if C < 0 then (iv) forces μ⌞M = 0.

3. (The tests vanish.) Let φ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ W. Pointwise φ(x)·f(x) = φ(x)·(θ(x)·g(x)) = θ(x)·(φ(x)·g(x)) by commutativity and associativity of the real product. Hence, by (v),
   ∫ φ(x)·f(x) d(μ⌞M)(x) = ∫_M θ(x)·(φ(x)·g(x)) dμ(x) = 0.

4. (Fundamental lemma.) The hypotheses of Mathlib's IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero hold for the open set W, the measure μ⌞M and the function f:
   - ℝ^P is a finite-dimensional real normed space with its Borel σ-algebra;
   - f is locally integrable on W for μ⌞M (step 2);
   - ∫ φ·f d(μ⌞M) = 0 for every C^∞ compactly supported φ with tsupport φ ⊆ W (step 3).
   The lemma requires no finiteness property of the measure. It gives: for μ⌞M-a.e. x, x ∈ W ⇒ θ(x)·g(x) = 0.

5. (Removing the weight.) M is μ-null-measurable, so μ⌞M-a.e. x lies in M (Mathlib ae_restrict_mem₀). Take x in the intersection of this full-measure set with the one from step 4, and suppose x ∈ W. Then θ(x)·g(x) = 0, and θ(x) > 0 by (i) because x ∈ M. So θ(x) ≠ 0 and g(x) = 0. Hence for μ⌞M-a.e. x, x ∈ W ⇒ g(x) = 0. ∎

```lean
theorem iwl_sp_sn_weighted_fundamental_lemma : ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (M W : Set (Eucl P)) (θ g : Eucl P → ℝ) (C : ℝ), IsOpen W → NullMeasurableSet M μ → (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x) → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ W) μ → AEStronglyMeasurable g (μ.restrict M) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict M), |g x| ≤ C) → (∀ φ : Eucl P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) φ → HasCompactSupport φ → tsupport φ ⊆ W → ∫ x in M, θ x * (φ x * g x) ∂μ = 0) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict M), x ∈ W → g x = 0 := by
  intro P μ M W θ g C hW hM hpos hθ hg hgC hint
  have hfint : IntegrableOn (fun x => θ x * g x) W (μ.restrict M) := by
    rw [IntegrableOn, Measure.restrict_restrict hW.measurableSet, Set.inter_comm]
    have hθ' : Integrable θ (μ.restrict (M ∩ W)) := hθ
    have hg' : AEStronglyMeasurable g (μ.restrict (M ∩ W)) :=
      hg.mono_measure (Measure.restrict_mono Set.inter_subset_left le_rfl)
    have hgC' : ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict (M ∩ W)), ‖g x‖ ≤ C := by
      have := ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset (Set.inter_subset_left : M ∩ W ⊆ M) hgC
      filter_upwards [this] with x hx
      simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs] using hx
    exact hθ'.mul_bdd hg' hgC'
  have hzero := hW.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero hfint.locallyIntegrableOn
    (fun φ hφ hφc hφW => by
      rw [← hint φ hφ hφc hφW]
      refine integral_congr_ae (Eventually.of_forall fun x => ?_)
      simp only [smul_eq_mul]
      ring)
  filter_upwards [hzero, ae_restrict_mem₀ hM] with x hx hxM hxW
  rcases mul_eq_zero.mp (hx hxW) with h | h
  · exact absurd h (hpos x hxM).ne'
  · exact h
```
proof_key_steps: (μ⌞M)⌞W = μ⌞(M ∩ W), because W is open (Measure.restrict_restrict).
θ·g is integrable there (Integrable.mul_bdd): θ is integrable, and g is a.e.-strongly measurable with |g| ≤ C a.e. Hence θ·g is locally integrable on W for μ⌞M.
For every C^∞ compactly supported φ with tsupport φ ⊆ W, ∫ φ·(θg) d(μ⌞M) = ∫_M θ·(φg) dμ = 0.
The fundamental lemma IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero, which holds for an arbitrary measure, gives θg = 0 μ⌞M-a.e. on W.
μ⌞M-a.e. x lies in M (ae_restrict_mem₀), where θ > 0. Hence g = 0 μ⌞M-a.e. on W.

subproblems.title: A rectifiable representation has Hⁿ-null carrier on each relatively compact open set where the current vanishes
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = tauAction n M θ ξ ω) → IsOpen W → IsCompact (closure W) → closure W ⊆ U → T.VanishesOn W → (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) (M ∩ W) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 3–7 of the parent proof, for one fixed open set W. The pieces come from siblings:
- the pointwise algebra of step 1 is the sibling signed_simple_bound (iwl_sp_sn_signed_simpleNVector_bound_ne_zero);
- the finite basis of step 2 is the sibling covector_basis (iwl_sp_sn_covector_separating_family);
- the analytic core of steps 4 and 6 is the sibling weighted_fundamental_lemma (iwl_sp_sn_weighted_fundamental_lemma).

Conventions.
- μ := μHE[n] = Hⁿ on ℝ^P = Eucl P, and ν := μ⌞M = μ.restrict M.
- Fields of IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ used below:
  - nullMeasurableSet: M is μ-null-measurable;
  - pos: θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M;
  - integrableOn: θ is μ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U;
  - aestronglyMeasurable: ξ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable;
  - orients: for ν-a.e. x there is an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ. Its tangent-space clause is not used.
- Dⁿ(U) = TestFormOn U n consists of the maps ω : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) n that are C^∞ (IsSmoothForm ω, i.e. ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) ω), have compact support, and satisfy tsupport ω ⊆ U.
- tauAction n M θ ξ ω = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x).

1. (Good points.) By orients, for ν-a.e. x there is an orthonormal τ with ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ. For each such x, apply the sibling signed_simple_bound to τ and w := ξ(x): |ξ(x)(b)| ≤ ‖b‖ for every n-covector b, and ξ(x) ≠ 0. Hence for ν-a.e. x, both (∀ b, |ξ(x)(b)| ≤ ‖b‖) and ξ(x) ≠ 0 hold.

2. (θ is integrable on M ∩ W, and W ⊆ U.) K := closure W is compact and K ⊆ U, so θ is μ-integrable on M ∩ K (integrableOn). Since W ⊆ closure W, M ∩ W ⊆ M ∩ K, so θ is μ-integrable on M ∩ W (IntegrableOn.mono_set). Also W ⊆ closure W ⊆ U.

3. (Coefficients.) Fix α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n and put g_α(x) := ξ(x)(α).
   - Evaluation at α, w ↦ w(α), is a continuous linear map NVector (Eucl P) n → ℝ (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ α). Composing it with ξ (aestronglyMeasurable) shows that g_α is ν-a.e. strongly measurable.
   - By step 1, |g_α(x)| ≤ ‖α‖ for ν-a.e. x.

4. (Testing T.) Let φ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ W. Define ω(x) := φ(x)·α.
   - ω is C^∞, as a smooth scalar function times a constant covector (ContDiff.smul with contDiff_const).
   - ω has compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right).
   - tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ W ⊆ U (tsupport_smul_subset_left and step 2).
   So ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W, and T(ω) = 0 because T vanishes on W. By linearity of ξ(x), ξ(x)(φ(x)·α) = φ(x)·g_α(x). The representation hypothesis then gives
   0 = T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(φ(x)·α) dμ(x) = ∫_M θ(x)·(φ(x)·g_α(x)) dμ(x).

5. (Each coefficient vanishes a.e. on W.) Apply the sibling weighted_fundamental_lemma with the measure μ, the sets M and W, the weight θ, g := g_α and C := ‖α‖. Its hypotheses hold:
   - W is open;
   - M is μ-null-measurable (nullMeasurableSet);
   - θ > 0 on M (pos);
   - θ is μ-integrable on M ∩ W (step 2);
   - g_α is ν-a.e. strongly measurable and |g_α| ≤ ‖α‖ ν-a.e. (step 3);
   - the test integrals vanish (step 4).
   Hence for ν-a.e. x, x ∈ W ⇒ ξ(x)(α) = 0.

6. (A finite separating family.) By the sibling covector_basis there are N ∈ ℕ and covectors b_1, …, b_N such that every n-vector vanishing on all b_i is zero. Apply step 5 to α = b_i for each of the finitely many i and intersect the full-measure sets (ae_all_iff). Then for ν-a.e. x, for every i, x ∈ W ⇒ ξ(x)(b_i) = 0.

7. (ν(W) = 0.) Take x in the intersection of the full-measure sets of steps 1 and 6, and suppose x ∈ W. Then ξ(x)(b_i) = 0 for every i, so ξ(x) = 0 by the separating property of step 6. This contradicts ξ(x) ≠ 0 from step 1. Hence ν-a.e. x satisfies x ∉ W, i.e. ν({x : x ∈ W}) = ν(W) = 0 (ae_iff).

8. (Conclusion.) W is open, hence measurable, so ν(W) = μ(W ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_apply). Therefore Hⁿ(M ∩ W) = μ(W ∩ M) = 0. ∎

The comparator's generated NodeSolution module (`exact Submission.iwl_sp_sn_local_null`) typechecks.

```lean
theorem iwl_sp_sn_local_null : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = tauAction n M θ ξ ω) → IsOpen W → IsCompact (closure W) → closure W ⊆ U → T.VanishesOn W → (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) (M ∩ W) = 0 := by
  intro P n U W T M θ ξ h hrep hWo hWc hWU hvan
  have hWU' : W ⊆ U := subset_closure.trans hWU
  have hθ : IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ W) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) :=
    (h.integrableOn (closure W) hWc hWU).mono_set (Set.inter_subset_inter_right M subset_closure)
  have hgood : ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M),
      (∀ b : Covector (Eucl P) n, |ξ x b| ≤ ‖b‖) ∧ ξ x ≠ 0 := by
    filter_upwards [h.orients] with x hx
    obtain ⟨τ, hτ, -, hξ⟩ := hx
    exact iwl_sp_sn_signed_simpleNVector_bound_ne_zero P n τ (ξ x) hτ hξ
  have key : ∀ α : Covector (Eucl P) n,
      ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), x ∈ W → ξ x α = 0 := by
    intro α
    refine iwl_sp_sn_weighted_fundamental_lemma P (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) M W θ
      (fun x => ξ x α) ‖α‖ hWo h.nullMeasurableSet h.pos hθ ?_ ?_ ?_
    · exact (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ α).continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable
        h.aestronglyMeasurable
    · filter_upwards [hgood] with x hx
      exact hx.1 α
    · intro φ hφ hφc hφW
      let ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n := fun x => φ x • α
      have hωs : IsSmoothForm ω := hφ.smul contDiff_const
      have hωc : HasCompactSupport ω := hφc.smul_right
      have hωW : tsupport ω ⊆ W := (tsupport_smul_subset_left φ (fun _ => α)).trans hφW
      let ωU : TestFormOn U n := ⟨ω, ⟨hωs, hωc⟩, hωW.trans hWU'⟩
      have h0 : T ωU = 0 := hvan ωU hωW
      rw [hrep ωU] at h0
      simpa [tauAction, ωU, ω, map_smul, smul_eq_mul] using h0
  obtain ⟨N, b, hb⟩ := iwl_sp_sn_covector_separating_family P n
  have hall : ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), ∀ i, x ∈ W → ξ x (b i) = 0 :=
    ae_all_iff.mpr (fun i => key (b i))
  have hnotW : ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), x ∉ W := by
    filter_upwards [hall, hgood] with x hx hg hxW
    exact hg.2 (hb (ξ x) (fun i => hx i hxW))
  have hres : (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M W = 0 := by
    rw [ae_iff] at hnotW
    simpa using hnotW
  rw [Measure.restrict_apply hWo.measurableSet, Set.inter_comm] at hres
  exact hres
```
proof_key_steps: Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x is good: by orients and signed_simple_bound, |ξ(x)(b)| ≤ ‖b‖ for every covector b, and ξ(x) ≠ 0.
θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ W ⊆ M ∩ closure W, because closure W is a compact subset of U.
For each covector α, testing T with φ·α (φ ∈ C_c^∞, tsupport φ ⊆ W) gives ∫_M θ·(φ·ξ(α)) dHⁿ = T(φα) = 0.
weighted_fundamental_lemma (g = ξ(·)(α), C = ‖α‖) gives ξ(x)(α) = 0 for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x ∈ W.
covector_basis plus finitely many a.e. sets give ξ = 0 a.e. on W. This contradicts ξ ≠ 0, so (Hⁿ⌞M)(W) = Hⁿ(M ∩ W) = 0.
